title: Premium Waivers: American Indian and Alaska Native Members and Financial Hardship
content:
A premium waiver on the Medicaid Managed Care Membership removes a billed coverage month from the family premium account with a recorded waiver reason, and there are two waiver reasons.

## American Indian or Alaska Native members

Members whose membership records them as American Indian or Alaska Native are never billed a premium. A month billed to such a member in error is waived in full with the waiver reason American Indian or Alaska Native.

## Financial hardship

A family facing a financial hardship may have billed months waived with the waiver reason financial hardship.

**What the caller must state.** A hardship waiver requires the parent or guardian to state a qualifying hardship during the call. The qualifying hardships are:

1. loss of employment;
2. a drop in household income of at least 20 percent;
3. unreimbursed medical expenses in the household.

The hardship is taken from what the parent or guardian states on the call; it is tied to the membership and to the coverage month being waived.

**Limit.** Hardship waivers are limited to the category's hardship waiver month limit within the 12 coverage months ending with the coverage month being waived, both ends included, counting the financial hardship waivers already recorded on the membership for coverage months in that span. A month beyond the limit is not waived and stays due.

## Rules for every waiver

- **Waiver or payment, not both.** Waiver and payment are mutually exclusive for one coverage month: a month already paid in full is not waived, and a waived month does not accept a payment.
- **Whole month only.** A waiver always covers the whole billed amount of the month, never part of it.

## Hardship statement check

| Stated on the call | Qualifying hardship |
|---|---|
| The parent lost a job | Yes |
| Household income fell by 20 percent | Yes (at least 20 percent) |
| Household income fell by 25 percent | Yes |
| Household income fell by 19 percent, with no other hardship stated | Not under the income-drop hardship |
| The household has unreimbursed medical expenses | Yes |

## Hypothetical limit cases

*Hypothetical, for a category whose hardship waiver month limit is 3.* The family asks to waive the March coverage month for financial hardship; the span read is April of the previous year through March.

- Financial hardship waivers are already recorded for two coverage months in that span. March would be the third, within the limit of 3.
- Financial hardship waivers are already recorded for three coverage months in that span. March is beyond the limit, is not waived and stays due.
- A waiver recorded for the previous February lies outside the span and is not counted.
